State Bank Of India vs Shakuntala Mehtani on 8 October, 2026

 STATE BANK OF INDIA VS. SHAKUNTALA MEHTANI

 IN THE DELHI STATE CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL
 COMMISSION

 Date of Institution: 05.12.2025
 Date of Hearing: 17.09.2026
 Date of Decision: 08.10.2026

 FIRST APPEAL NO. - 601/2025

 IN THE MATTER OF

 STATE BANK OF INDIA,
 THROUGH CHIEF MANAGER,
 40-41, BAKSHI HOUSE,
 NEHRU PLACE, NEW DELHI-110019.

 (Through: Mr. Rajiv B. Samaiyar and
 Ms. Akanksha Ahuja, Advocates)

 ...Appellant
 VERSUS

 MS. SHAKUNTALA MEHTANI,
 (SENIOR CITIZEN),
 W/O SH. R.C MEHTANI,
 R/O C-4/52,
 SAFDERJUNG DEVELOPMENT AREA,
 NEW DELHI-110016.
 ...Respondent

DISMISSED PAGE 1 OF 12
 FA/601/2025 D.O.D.: 08.10.2026
 STATE BANK OF INDIA VS. SHAKUNTALA MEHTANI

 CORAM:
 HON'BLE JUSTICE SANGITA DHINGRA SEHGAL (PRESIDENT)
 HON'BLE MS. BIMLA KUMARI, MEMBER (FEMALE)

 Present: Mr. Rajiv B. Samiyar appeared through VC and Ms. Akanksha Ahuja
 counsel for the Appellant.
 Mr. Raj Vardhan, counsel for the Respondent.

 PER: HON'BLE JUSTICE SANGITA DHINGRA SEHGAL, PRESIDENT

 JUDGMENT
1. The facts of the case as per the District Commission record are as under:
"Complainant has filed the present complaint seeking
 direction to OP to refund sum of Rs.42,92,450/-
 withdrawn unauthorisedly due to deficient and
 negligent services of OP; to pay a sum of
 Rs.20,00,000/- towards physical and mental agony
 and harassment caused to the complainant; to award
 the cost of litigation.
1. It is stated that complainant is a senior citizen and
 an old customer of State Bank of India hereinafter
 referred to as OP. It is further stated that on
 16.07.2021 there were unauthorised and fraudulent
 withdrawals from the Saving Account
 No.56189023119 and Over Draft Account
 No.56189003771 due to the connivance of (Shri Ajay
 Kumar Manchanda, (ex-Accountant of the
 complainant) with unknown bank officers of OP.
DISMISSED PAGE 2 OF 12
 FA/601/2025 D.O.D.: 08.10.2026
STATE BANK OF INDIA VS. SHAKUNTALA MEHTANI
2. It is next stated that OP officials procrastinated on
 the matter for many months on the pretext that
 complaint is forwarded to controlling office on where
 it was said to be pending.
3. It is further stated that complainant came to know
 that approximately sum of Rs.3,33,450/- was
 fraudulently withdrawn from her Savings Account
 and approximately sum of Rs.39,59,000/- from OD.
 Account without her knowledge and consent.
4. It is next stated that upon asking Shri Ajay Kumar
 Manchanda, ex-Accountant of the complainant he
 confessed that he changed complainant's all personal
 details like email, phone number etc. to his email and
 mobile number for the purpose of transaction alerts,
 OTPs with the help of his acquaintances who were
 employees of State Bank of India.
5. It is stated that complainant's accounts had only
 'View Only option and was not activated or
 authorised by her for online transactions. Upon
 having knowledge of the fraud committed
 complainant and her husband personally visited the
 bank to make a formal complaint which was refused
 by OP.
6. Therefore the complainant was constrained to send
 the complainant dated 16.07.2021 by email and
 courier/speed post. Complainant also lodged an FIR

DISMISSED PAGE 3 OF 12
 FA/601/2025 D.O.D.: 08.10.2026
 STATE BANK OF INDIA VS. SHAKUNTALA MEHTANI

 on 27.12.2021 against the ex-Accountant and
 employees of OP of Nehru Place Branch and the same
 is pending investigation.
7. Alleging deficiency of service complainant has
 approached this Commission.
8. ⁠OP resisted the complaint stating interalia that
 complainant has not come to the Commission with
 clean hands. Complainant has suppressed her part of
 negligence which caused the alleged unauthorised
 transactions.
9. ⁠It is stated that complainant is using internet
 banking services since 21.02.2018 and has given
 access of her account to third party. All the alleged
 transactions were done by him from the complainant's
 account.
10. It is further stated that complaint is not
 maintainable for misjoinder of party as complainant
 has made allegations against Mr. Ajay Kumar
 Manchanda, however, same has not been made party
 in the complaint.
11. It is further stated that complainant has alleged
 that her ex-accountant had fraudulently withdrawn
 the amount as per the complainant whose had the
 facility of "view only" on her internet banking,
 lodging the FIR and complained after lapse of more
 than 1.5 years from the alleged incident is not justified.
DISMISSED PAGE 4 OF 12
 FA/601/2025 D.O.D.: 08.10.2026
STATE BANK OF INDIA VS. SHAKUNTALA MEHTANI
12. It is next stated that upon the complaint filed by
 the complainant OP sent it to the Fraud Monitoring
 Cell of the Local Head Office, New Delhi, to
 investigate the same. After investigation it was found
 that there was no connivance of any officials of OP.
 It is stated that OP as per the request, provided the
 internet banking facility to the complainant and the
 transaction alerts were duly received by the
 complainant on her registered mobile number
 therefore the allegations made by the complainant are
 not sustainable.
13. It is stated that the mobile number could be
 changed only after getting mandate from the customer.
 In light of the same, it is prayed that the instant
 complaint be dismissed."
2. The District Commission after taking into consideration the material available on
 record passed the order dated 11.08.2025, whereby it held as under:
"Status report dated 08.05.2023 filed by the IO
 before the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi is perused.
 It is noted that case against the ex-accountant Shri
 Ajay Kumar Manchanda is pending before the Trial
 Court. Investigation regarding the role of bank
 officials, disposal of cheated amount was still in
 progress. It is seen from the status report filed by the
 police before the Hon'ble Delhi High Court that the

DISMISSED PAGE 5 OF 12
 FA/601/2025 D.O.D.: 08.10.2026
 STATE BANK OF INDIA VS. SHAKUNTALA MEHTANI

 accountant of the complainant could get the
 registered mobile number of the complainant
 changed with the help of OP bank's clerk namely
 Ajay Kumar Kaushal. It was also found out from the
 enquiries made by the police that the written consent
 of the customer is mandatory for change of
 registered mobile number however request in the
 present matter is not available with the bank.
Further, it is noted from the WS filed by the OP on
 record that in reply to para 5 of the complaint, OP
 has confirmed that mobile number could be changed
 only after getting mandate from the customer.
 However, it is seen that OP has not placed any
 document to show that there a mandate was given by
 the complainant to change her mobile number.
It is also seen that complainant has alleged that she
 was using the internet banking facility as view only
 option but the transactions were done using the
 internet facility for which the OP has not given any
 cogent reason as to the circumstances under which
 the said mandate was changed and whether it was
 done as per rules.
It is also seen that OP has not filed any documents
 on record to support any of their contentions. An
 evasive reply is given by the OP stating that option

DISMISSED PAGE 6 OF 12
 FA/601/2025 D.O.D.: 08.10.2026
 STATE BANK OF INDIA VS. SHAKUNTALA MEHTANI

 of Internet banking facility was given to the
 complainant and that the alerts were duly received
 by the complainant on her registered mobile number.
 The reply fails to clarify anything about the change
 of the registered mobile number and the process
 undertaken to change the registered mobile number
 because of which the complainant lost huge sum of
 money.
It is further seen that though OP has categorically
 denied hand of any of their employees in this entire
 activity, the police inquiry report clearly indicates
 not just the hand but also the name of the banking
 official who had helped the accountant of the
 complainant to get away with the change of
 registered mobile number because of which the
 accountant could withdraw huge amount of money
 from the account of the complainant to his own
 account. Further, the OP states that they conducted
 an enquiry but the report of it has not been placed
 on record.
All these facts coupled with the fact that OP has not
 placed on record any evidence to prove their stand
 of sticking to the mandate provided in respect of
 change of mobile number and change in internet
 banking facility, this Commission is of the view that
 OP has been deficient in its services. Had the OP

DISMISSED PAGE 7 OF 12
 FA/601/2025 D.O.D.: 08.10.2026
 STATE BANK OF INDIA VS. SHAKUNTALA MEHTANI

 bank followed the mandate and sought for the
 written consent of the complainant for changing her
 mobile number to another mobile number the money
 of the complainant could have been protected.
This Commission therefore directs the OP to pay
 42,92,450/-lost by the complainant into her account
 with interest at 7% per annum from the date of each
 transaction. OP is further directed to pay a sum of
 Rs.1,00,000 as compensation to the complainant for
 the harassment caused to a senior citizen and who
 was made to run from pillar to post for her own
 money. This order is to be complied with within three
 months from the date of the pronouncement of the
 order failing which the interest payable would be 9%
 per annum till realization."
3. Aggrieved by the aforesaid order of the District Commission, the Appellant has
 preferred the present appeal contending that the District Commission has erred
 in holding the deficiency of service on the part of the Appellant and in directing
 payment of Rs. 42,92,450/- along with interest and compensation. The Appellant
 further submitted that the District Commission failed to consider the fact that the
 alleged transactions were carried out by the erstwhile accountant of the
 Respondent, Shri Ajay Kumar Manchanda, who, as per the case of the
 Respondent, had access to the accounts and had changed the registered mobile
 number and other personal details. The Appellant has also submitted that the
 internet banking facility could not have been upgraded from "View Only" to a
 transaction-enabled facility without the mandate of the account holder and that

DISMISSED PAGE 8 OF 12
 FA/601/2025 D.O.D.: 08.10.2026
 STATE BANK OF INDIA VS. SHAKUNTALA MEHTANI

 the transaction alerts were duly sent to the registered mobile number. It has also
 been submitted that, upon receipt of the complaint, the matter was referred to the
 Fraud Monitoring Cell, which found no connivance of any official of the
 Appellant Bank. The Appellant has relied upon the RBI guidelines dated
 06.07.2017 concerning customer protection in unauthorized electronic banking
 transactions and contended that the Respondent failed to establish any negligence
 or deficiency on the part of the Bank. Pressing the aforesaid submissions, the
 Appellants have prayed for setting aside the impugned order passed by the
 District Commission.
4. Vide order dated 04.08.2026, Counsel appearing on behalf of the Respondent
 submitted that the Respondent does not wish to file a reply or written arguments
 and would make oral submissions before this Commission.
5. We have perused the material available on record and heard the counsel appeared
 on behalf of the Appellant and the Respondent.
6. The main question for consideration before us is whether the District
 Commission erred in holding the Appellant deficient in service and in directing
 the Appellant to reimburse a sum of Rs.42,92,450/- along with interest and
 compensation to the Respondent.
7. On perusal of the record, we find that the Respondent had specifically alleged
 that the registered mobile number linked with the bank accounts was changed
 without her knowledge or consent and that the internet banking facility, which
 was stated to be limited to "View Only", was subsequently utilized for carrying
 out the disputed transactions. The Appellant, on the other hand, has contended
 that the change in the registered mobile number and the activation of the
 transaction facility could not have been affected without the mandate of the
 account holder. However, despite taking such a specific stand, the Appellant has
 failed to place on record any document evidencing the mandate or written consent

DISMISSED PAGE 9 OF 12
 FA/601/2025 D.O.D.: 08.10.2026
 STATE BANK OF INDIA VS. SHAKUNTALA MEHTANI

 of the Respondent for change of the registered mobile number or for alteration of
 the internet banking facility.
8. It is further evident from the record that the Status Report dated 08.05.2023
 submitted by the Investigating Officer before the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi
 records that the registered mobile number of the Respondent was changed with
 the assistance of an official of the Appellant Bank. The said report further
 indicates that written consent of the customer was mandatory for such change,
 whereas no such request was available with the Bank. Thus, the material available
 on record raises a serious question regarding compliance with the prescribed
 banking procedure by the Appellant.
9. Furthermore, the submission of the Appellant that transaction alerts were duly
 received on the registered mobile number also does not satisfactorily explain the
 circumstances in which the registered mobile number itself came to be changed.
 Once the Appellant admitted that change of the registered mobile number
 required a mandate from the account holder, it was incumbent upon the Appellant
 to produce the relevant mandate or other contemporaneous record to establish
 that the change was duly authorized. However, no such material has been filed
 by the Appellant before the District Commission as well as before this
 Commission.
10. Similarly, the Appellant has failed to produce any cogent material to establish
 when and in what manner the internet banking facility was upgraded from "View
 Only" to a transaction-enabled facility and pursuant to whose request or
 authorization such change was effected. Additionally, the Appellant being the
 custodian of the relevant banking records was in a position to produce such
 material and the failure to produce the same assumes significance when the
 disputed transactions were carried out thereafter and the Respondent has
 consistently denied having authorized such transactions.
DISMISSED PAGE 10 OF 12
 FA/601/2025 D.O.D.: 08.10.2026
STATE BANK OF INDIA VS. SHAKUNTALA MEHTANI
11. The Appellant has also relied upon the RBI guidelines dated 06.07.2017 relating
 to customer protection in unauthorized electronic banking transactions. However,
 before seeking to attribute liability to the Respondent, the Appellant was required
 to establish the circumstances in which the disputed transactions were
 authenticated and to demonstrate compliance with the prescribed procedure. The
 Appellant has failed to establish that the Respondent had authorized the change
 of the registered mobile number or the alteration of the internet banking facility.
 The mere fact that the transactions were carried out through internet banking or
 that alerts were generated on the registered mobile number cannot, in the
 circumstances of the present case, establish authorization by the Respondent.
12. In view of the aforesaid discussion, it is clear that the Appellant Bank failed to
 establish that the change of the registered mobile number and the alteration of the
 internet banking facility were carried out pursuant to a valid mandate or consent
 of the Respondent. The Appellant also failed to produce the relevant banking
 records or the internal investigation report to substantiate its defense.
13. In these circumstances, we are of the considered view that the Appellant Bank
 was deficient in providing its banking services and failed to exercise the requisite
 care and diligence expected from it, which resulted in the unauthorized
 withdrawal of the amount from the accounts of the Respondent. The finding of
 deficiency in service recorded by the District Commission, therefore, does not
 call for any interference.
14. In view of the foregoing, we are in agreement with the reasons given by the
 District Commission and fail to find any cause or reason to reverse the findings
 of the District Commission. Consequently, we uphold the order dated
 11.08.2025 passed by the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum-II,
 (South District), GNCT of Delhi, Udyog Sadan, C-22 & 23, Qutub Institutional
 Area (Behind Qutub Hotel), New Delhi -110016.
DISMISSED PAGE 11 OF 12
 FA/601/2025 D.O.D.: 08.10.2026
STATE BANK OF INDIA VS. SHAKUNTALA MEHTANI
15. Consequently, the present Appeal stands dismissed with no order as to costs.
16. Application(s) pending, if any, stand disposed of in terms of the aforesaid
 judgment.
17. The Judgment be uploaded forthwith on the website of the Commission for the
 perusal of the parties.
18. File be consigned to record room along with a copy of this Judgment.
(JUSTICE SANGITA DHINGRA SEHGAL)
 PRESIDENT
